chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Jibra'il (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Muhammad, live as you wish for you will indeed die, love whomever you wish for you will indeed be separated from them, do as you wish for you will indeed be requited for it, and act as you wish for you will surely meet it [in the Hereafter].' Ibn Abi Umayr said, 'Ibn Sinan added to it: O Muhammad, the honor of a believer is his night prayer, and his esteem is his refraining from harming people.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Angel Jibra'il tell Prophet Muhammad about death and the Hereafter?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the reliable chain of Ibn Abi Umair and Ibn Sinan, presents a fourfold imperative from Jibra'il that balances worldly detachment with spiritual accountability, a theme central to Shia asceticism (zuhd). The addition by Ibn Sinan specifically links the believer's nobility to nocturnal devotion (tahajjud) and social grace, reflecting the Imami emphasis on combining inner piety with outward ethical conduct. This narrative serves as a foundational text for understanding the Prophetic model of balancing the transient nature of life with the eternal reality of the Hereafter.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 7.Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) who said,

“Jibraʾīl (a) came to the Prophet (ṣ) and said, ‘O Muḥammad, live as you like for you will indeed die, love whomever you want for you will indeed separate, do whatever you wish for you will indeed be requited therefor, and act however you wish for you will surely meet it [in the Hereafter].’” Ibn Abī ʿUmayr said, “Ibn Sinān added [one more phrase] to it, ‘O Muḥammad, the honor of a believer is [in] his prayer in the night, and his esteem is [in] his refraining from harming the people.’”
